1.
Heard learned senior counsel for the petitioners and the learned GP-4, Shri. Manish Kumar.

2. The learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the land in dispute pertains to Khata No. 95, Khesra No. 518 and 519 at Mauza-Pothia, Tauzi No. 1, Area- 2.73 acres,
District-Katihar.
3. The learned senior counsel for the petitioners next submits that the aforesaid land is recorded in the name of late Gopi Mohan Prasad, i.e., the petitioners' grandfather.
Late Gopi Mohan Prasad had a son, namely, late Sadanand Prasad, and late Sadanand Prasad had six sons, including the petitioners and petitioner of CWJC No. 9853 of 2023.

It is next submitted that Jamabandi No. 95 created in the name of late Gopi Mohan Prasad, with regard to the land in dispute, is still in existence and the raiyati rights over the land in dispute remained with the ancestors of the petitioners previously and now with the petitioners, i.e., the raiyati right in the land was never Patna High Court CWJC No.9853 of 2023(5) dt.04-03-2025 transferred outside the family.

4. It is further submitted that the land was located in an area which was prone to criminal activity,
endangering the life and property of the citizens of that vicinity, hence the ancestors of the petitioners permitted the police to do patrolling and other duties by utilizing some parts of 2.73 acres of land in dispute, but then it was a mere permission and no raiyati right in the land was ever transferred, either by the grandfather or the father of the petitioners in favour of the police.
5. It is next submitted that the police, for the purposes of maintaining law and order in the area,
constructed Pothia outposts on some portion of the land in dispute, without any permission from the petitioners' grandfather or father, and even without the permission of the Department of Home,

2 Government of Bihar.
6.

sentences.text: It is submitted that agricultural work over the land in dispute adjacent to the Pothia OP was being carried by the legal heirs of late Gopi Mohan Prasad for some time, but for the past some years, no agricultural work was being done because of the fact that legal heirs were in job.

7. It is further submitted that since for some years, the petitioners were not using the land for agricultural purposes, as Patna High Court CWJC No.9853 of 2023(5) dt.04-03-2025 such the land was lying fallow adjacent to Pothia OP, hence the police personnel posted at Pothia OP encroached the leftover land and made temporary arrangements over the major part of the land in dispute and slowly a permanent structure of outpost was created, without seeking permission either from the father of the petitioners or the petitioners and as such the police personnel have encroached the entire 2.73 acres of land in dispute and are not allowing the petitioners to carry out their agricultural activities after their retirement.

8. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State, at this stage, based on the pleadings made in the counter- affidavit filed on behalf of Respondent No. 7 and 8, submits that Pothia OP was constructed in the year 1918 and as such the petitioners or their ancestors never remained in possession over the land after 1918, nor they even made any endeavours to take possession of the land, nor after revisional survey operation ever paid any rent with respect to the land in dispute,
further the SHO, Pothia PS has been asked vide Letter No. 849 dated 16-5- 2023 to submit gift deed or any other document executed in favour of the Hon'ble Governor of Bihar, and the Revenue Officer was directed to search such transaction papers in the Registry Office, Purnia and Record Room, Purnia, but no paper Patna High Court CWJC No.9853 of 2023(5) dt.04-03-2025 could be made available.

9. The counter-affidavit at para-6 records that - land covering an area 2.73 acres admittedly stands recorded in the name of Gopi Mohan Prasad, as per Letter No. 1109 dated 17-6- 2023 issued by the Circle Officer, Falka, the name of the landholder Gopi Mohan Prasad has been mentioned in Jamabandi Panji, but the same has been surrounded by red ink mentioning the name of one Amrendra Madhav, but his name also has been surrounded by red ink
, further the words- "Thana makan evam stopped" has been mentioned in Jamabandi Panji, further in the right side of the page words -      acquired   ,   " , have been noted.

10. The learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that from perusal of the counter-affidavit, it becomes manifestly clear that the land in the RS Khatiyan was recorded in the name of Gopi Mohan Prasad, but his name and the name of Amrendra Madhav was surrounded by red ink, and it was recorded in the Jamabandi Register that the land was acquired for Pothia Thana, but then the counter-affidavit is completely silent that as to on what basis the land was acquired, as to the knowledge of the petitioners, no gift deed ever was executed by the ancestors of the petitioners with regard to the Patna High Court CWJC No.9853 of 2023(5) dt.04-03-2025 land in dispute, nor any acquisition proceeding under the Land Acquisition Act 1894 was ever resorted to.

It is next submitted that the land was never acquired, rather the same has been illegally encroached by the respondent authority in complete breach of the law, without paying any Manoj Madhav vs The State Of Bihar on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65542102/
3 compensation to the petitioners

sentences.text: , it is next submitted that had the land been acquired, in that event Jamabandi No. 95 in the name of Gopi Mohan Prasad would not have been in existence till date.
It is submitted that the fact that Jamabandi No. 95 is still existing, that in itself demonstrates the falsity of the pleadings made in the counter- affidavit.

11. The learned State counsel appearing in CWJC No. 9853 of 2023, submits that counter-affidavit on behalf of Respondent Nos. 7 and 8 has been filed, which is similar to the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of Respondent No. 7 and 8 in the instant writ petition, further a counter-affidavit on behalf of Respondent Nos. 2 and 6 has also been filed, the same more or less is in tune with the counter-affidavit of Respondent No. 7 and 8 in the instant case.

12. The learned senior counsel for the petitioners next submits that from perusal of the counter-affidavit filed in both the cases, it appears that the authorities are trying to raise an Patna High Court CWJC No.9853 of 2023(5) dt.04-03-2025 issue that the land in dispute is in their possession for the last 106 years, as such it is too late in the day for the petitioners to contend that the land belongs to them.

It is next submitted that the State will have to come out with a clear stand that what is the basis, based on which the State is claiming that the land belongs to them, if it is based on possession then whether the State can claim adverse possession against its own citizen.

13. The learned senior counsel for the petitioners next asserts and submits that neither the grandfather, late Gopi Mohan Prasad, nor the father of the petitioners ever executed any gift deed in the name of the Hon'ble Governor of Bihar with respect to the land in dispute.

14. It is next reiterated and submitted that no doubt the grandfather of the petitioners had permitted the police to use the land for the purposes of patrolling as the area was infested with criminals, but then that by no stretch of imagination can be construed that it was a gift in favor of the State, as there is no provision under the Transfer of Property Act to make oral gifts with respect to property belonging to Hindus and for that proposition relies on Section 122 of the Transfer of Property Act.

15. It is next submitted that the State is harping that the Patna High Court CWJC No.9853 of 2023(5) dt.04-03-2025 rent with respect to the land in dispute was not paid by the petitioners,
which amply demonstrates that the petitioners were never in possession of the land in dispute, but then the authorities have completely failed to appreciate that merely because rent of the land has not been paid that in no manner is an evidence to the fact that the petitioners have relinquished their claim over the land in dispute.
It is next submitted that if the rent has not been paid, the authorities have the power and jurisdiction to realize the rent of the land from the petitioners, in accordance with law.
It is also submitted that the fact that Jamabandi No. 95 is still in existence that amply demonstrates that the land was never acquired by the State or else jamabandi would have been cancelled.
16. It is reiterated and submitted at the cost of repetition that the State cannot claim adverse possession as it is a welfare State.

sentences.text: The learned State counsel seeks four weeks' further time to file a supplementary counter- affidavit.

18. The Court is not satisfied with the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of Respondent Nos. 2 and 6,
and 7 and 8 in CWJC No. 9853 of 2023 and the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of Respondent Nos.
7 and 8 in the instant writ petition, as Patna High Court CWJC No.9853 of 2023(5) dt.04-03-2025 such, the Court is not inclined to grant time to the State for filing a supplementary counter-affidavit,
but then directs the learned State counsel to file two separate counter-affidavits duly sworn by the Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Home, Government of Bihar, Patna and the Secretary,
Revenue and Land Reform Department, Government of Bihar.

The counter- affidavit shall give para-wise reply of the pleadings made in the writ application and shall also reply the contention of the petitioners as recorded in the instant order, i.e., whether the State can claim adverse possession against its own citizen and whether the State can acquire the raiyati lands of the petitioners without resorting to procedure established by law and also if jamabandi with respect to the land is still in existence, whether it does not point to the fact that the land in dispute has not been acquired.
19. Put up these cases on 15-4-2025.
20.
It is made clear that no further construction on the land in dispute shall be made by the authorities until and unless the writ application is finally adjudicated by this Court.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) SUMIT/-
